title: network-handoff-checklist-private-deployments-and-upgrade-ramps
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a compact, operational handoff and verification checklist for customer private deployments (VPC, VPC+DirectConnect/Interconnect, and air-gapped on-prem bundles). It focuses on the network and upgrade surface: what the SRE/onboarding engineer must validate before we hand traffic over and during each upgrade window. It is intentionally terse for use during calls and runbooks.

Audience:
- Solutions Engineer (SE) owning initial customer network setup
- Onboarding SRE who validates connectivity and performs cutover
- Customer network/security contacts
- Release engineer leading inference runtime upgrades

High-level acceptance criteria before first production traffic:
- Control plane connectivity: customer control-plane peering or VPN established and authenticated. TLS certs validated (expiry > 90 days).
- Data plane reachability: inference workers can reach model artifact storage endpoints and telemetry endpoints on required ports.
- Egress constraints: NAT / egress firewall rules allow Redwood outbound IPs or CIDR ranges used for pull/push.
- DNS resolution: internal hostnames resolvable per the agreed split-horizon plan; SRV/CAA records present if used.
- MTU and path MTU discovery: validated between customer edge and Redwood private endpoints (minimum 1400 for jumbo avoidance).
- Clock sync: NTP reachable or PTP validated for clusters (max drift < 250ms).

Quick checklist (call-ready):
- [ ] Confirm primary CIDR blocks and reserved ranges (list agreed excluded IPs).
- [ ] Confirm subnet map for worker vs control plane vs storage access.
- [ ] Confirm routing: static vs BGP (ASN pair) and advertised prefixes.
- [ ] Confirm NAT gateway behavior for egress and ephemeral port ranges.
- [ ] Confirm firewall / NGFW rules: ports 22, 443, 80, 10250 (k8s) allowed for required peers.
- [ ] Confirm KMS/HSM endpoints and key access policies.
- [ ] Validate logging: fluentd/collector endpoints reachable, TLS mutual-auth if enabled.
- [ ] Validate monitoring: metrics exporters and tracing ingestion endpoints accessible.
- [ ] Confirm backup/restore access to blob store or on-prem storage (S3-compatible endpoints).

Terraform module practical notes (observed patterns and gotchas):
- Use separate TF workspaces for network and runtime modules. Keep lifecycle for shared routes outside of per-tenant modules to avoid accidental deletion.
- When creating peerings, set explicit routes (route table attachments) rather than relying on implicit cloud-provider behavior; peerings are often order-sensitive in DR tests.
- Aim for immutable idempotent modules: avoid data sources that return different results across runs (use fixed tags/names in module inputs).
- For DirectConnect/Interconnect style setups, include BGP auth md5 optional parameter; many customers require it.
- Add optional argument for MTU override on tunnel resources (we've hit defaults of 1500 causing fragmentation with GRE overlays).
- Provide a toggle for creating a shared NAT vs per-subnet NAT to match customer egress policy.

Network topology variants (short):
- Minimal VPC-peering: single VPC peered to customer VPC; simple, lower ops, but needs explicit route table management and careful CIDR planning.
- Transit/Hub model: Redwood-provided transit VPC or TGW; supports many customers and central firewalling but requires TGW attachments and central route policies. Preferred for multiple private peers.
- Site-to-site with BGP: used for DC-style customers with VLANs; gives dynamic failover and path control.
- Air-gapped / on-prem appliance bundle: image-based runtime with inbound-only management via scheduled polling; requires special artifact replication plan and offline upgrade path.

Upgrade plan: safe rolling upgrade (example steps)
1) Pre-upgrade validation (2–3 days before):
   - Smoke tests run against staging replicas in customer network.
   - Verify snapshot of route tables, security group rules, and NAT entries captured in TF state.
   - Lock TF state for change window.
2) Prep window (2 hours before):
   - Increase logging level for upgrade path to capture transient failures.
   - Take backups of kv-store / model artifacts relevant to runtime.
   - Notify customer contacts and open dedicated Slack channel + incident bridge.
3) Canary batch (15–30m):
   - Deploy new runtime on 1 AZ / 10% of capacity.
   - Run a set of 20 canonical prompts and synthetic load at 2x p95 token rate.
   - Validate latency/throughput, KV cache warmup, and memory usage.
   - If regressions > predefined thresholds (latency +20% or error rate > 0.5%), auto rollback to previous image and abort ramp.
4) Progressive rollout (hourly steps):
   - Move traffic by weights (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with 15–30 minute observation windows.
   - Ensure model artifact checksums match expected values after each rollout step.
5) Post-upgrade validation (1–2h):
   - Run customer-specific eval set and smoke tests.
   - Confirm logging/metrics ingestion and removal of canary toggles.

Rollback triggers and immediate actions:
- Trigger conditions: >20% token latency regression, >1% error rate increase over baseline, or missing artifact pulls.
- Actions: scale down new variant nodes, route traffic to previous variant, collect heap/dump from failing nodes, notify customer, open postmortem ticket PD-8421.

Operational artifacts to collect during onboarding call:
- Terraform state export (redacted for secrets).
- BGP session logs and BGP peer config (ASN, MD5, hold timers).
- Route table snapshots (before/after).
- Firewall rule export (allow/deny lists).
- MTU/pathmtu test results (traceroute with packetsize).

Runbook snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- Verify BGP session:
  1) ssh to edge-router: show ip bgp summary | grep <peer-asn>
  2) confirm Established state and advertised prefixes count

- Quick NAT test (from worker node):
  curl -sS -I https://canary.redwood-inference.test --interface <egress-ip>

Common customer questions we should be prepared to answer:
- "What private IP ranges do you reserve?" -> Provide our reserved list (10.240.0.0/12 by default) and discuss overlap handling.
- "How do you handle data egress to third-party SaaS?" -> Describe egress proxy options and allowlist process.
- "Can we use our KMS/HSM?" -> Yes, provide KMS endpoints and IAM policy templates; note latency impacts for key ops.

Open engineering notes / TODOs for module owners:
- Add a boolean flag to disable automatic garbage collection of peerings in the network module.
- Add detailed CI tests that simulate BGP flap and assert route stability.
- Improve error messages when TF apply fails due to missing route table dependencies.
- Document air-gapped artifact sync tooling and add checksum verification step.

Appendix: useful links and references
- Confluence: PRIVATE VPC ARCH (see linked_artifacts above)
- GitHub: repo infra/modules/network (PR: gh-1973)
- Jira: PD-8421 (upgrade postmortem template)

Notes-to-self (choppy, keep):
- Ask legal if we can publish simplified CIDR example for small customers.
- Follow up w/ security on default firewall egress rules.

End of doc.
